about_this_file: The promise to the people who are called. The text of each line is PLAN.md section 5, word for word. Each line has an id (P1..P12) and a slug the baseline checks after every release (TEAM.md item P6). A line that names a human is published only when ops/HUMAN_JOBS.md names that human; until then it says 'reviewed by the operator'. The checks run in the release checks after every deploy.
source: PLAN.md section 5 'The promise'; TEAM.md section 5 item P6

lines.text: Before you take a call you see who answers for it, that an AI is asking, how long it takes, what it pays, how it is rated, and what will be recorded.
lines.check: GET /v1/seats/{token} returns, before the seat is taken: who answers for the call, asker_is_ai true, minutes, pay or 'UNPAID TEST', content rating, what will be recorded.
baseline_lines: the ring card has every field before the seat is taken

lines.text: You can decline, or stop partway, with no mark against you. You are paid from the first second.
lines.check: A seat stopped at 40 seconds is paid for 40 seconds; declining leaves no field on the person that a later call reads.

lines.text: An offer is held for you. You never open a call that is already full.
lines.check: A seat offered is held for one person for a minute; a full call never shows its link (take returns 409 and the page says so before any work).
baseline_lines: a full call is never offered to another member

lines.text: No asker can reject your work. Pay is withheld only for proven fraud, shown to you, with an appeal.
lines.check: Marking a response 'not counted' leaves its pay and its receipt unchanged; no asker operation withholds pay.

lines.text: You are never made to do an unpaid screener.
lines.check: Every question a person answers before or during a call is inside a paid (or declared UNPAID TEST) seat; no question is asked before the seat is taken.

lines.text: You see what the asker paid and what each fee was.
lines.check: The person's receipt lists what the asker paid and each fee line, matching the ledger.

lines.text: Your receipts are yours. Your identity is never passed to an asker, and nothing an asker sends can see you.
lines.check: The asker's result holds no name, contact or device identity; the asker's server gets no request from the runner; material is served from our own storage.

lines.text: Your voice is yours: the asker gets your words, and the recording only if you say yes for that call.
lines.check: The asker's result holds no recording unless that person said yes for that call.

lines.text: You choose when you can be rung, and never at night unless you say so.
lines.check: No ring inside a person's quiet hours (9 PM to 8 AM where they are by default) or while they are Off; a call opened at 3 AM rings nobody and its quote says when it will.
baseline_lines: fence: no ring in quiet hours (3 AM local)

lines.text: You can leave and take your data with you, or have it deleted, in one tap.
lines.check: One tap, after an offer to save receipts, deletes the account, recordings, answers and record; a lookup afterwards finds nothing.

lines.text: You can report any call, and it stops.
lines.check: 'Stop: this upset me' and 'report this call' stop the call for everyone and create a report a human reads.

lines.text: Where the asker tells us, you see what your answer changed.
lines.check: A line the asker sends back about what it did with the answers is screened and appears on each person's receipt.

also: On a panel of fewer than five, both sides are told that answers cannot be anonymous.
A line that names a human ('a person decides your appeal') is published only when ops/HUMAN_JOBS.md names that human; until then the words are 'reviewed by the operator'.
baseline_rule: A line counts as 'checked after every release' only when every baseline line listed for it passed in the newest bin/baseline run that ran to its end, whichever project's deploy ran it. The lists are exact baseline line names; [P<n>] tags in line names win where a line carries one. P7 has three clauses: identity (a [P7] line: the asker's result holds no identity), 'nothing an asker sends can see you' ([P7 part] lines: the call page reaches only our own address, a whole call makes no outside request) and 'your receipts are yours' (a [P10 part] line: the person saves every receipt); all three pass in the 09:13Z baseline, so the count of 12 holds only while all of them pass. The result is written to canon/out/promise_status.json, which every page reads. Tags: '[Pn]' on a passing line checks the whole of Pn; '[Pn part]' checks only part and never counts the promise; any failing '[Pn]' or '[Pn part]' line uncounts it (a broken part breaks the promise). Lines may be printed as 'PROMISE PASS ...'.
